subject: Follow-up: Dedicated capacity sizing — scenario confirmation & proposed slots
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Samir Kapadia <samir@cloudledger.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 28 Nov 2027 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: Dedicated capacity sizing — scenario confirmation & proposed slots

Hi Samir —

Great to meet today. Quick recap from our discovery so we’re aligned ahead of the sizing session: 

- Goals: deploy a dedicated pool to serve internal and customer-facing inference for invoices and audit-search (latency SLOs for UI < 200ms p95, batch export throughput for nightly jobs).
- Primary workloads: interactive chat-like queries (avg request length 350 tokens, bursts up to 40 qps for short windows) and nightly batch reranking (peak sustained 300 qps for 2 hours).
- Data constraints: model inputs include customer PII; CloudLedger needs VPC/private deployment and audit logs retained 12 months.

Ask: before we lock the slot, can you confirm the following numbers from your side?
1) Expected steady-state interactive qps (avg and 95th percentile)
2) Max simultaneous KV cache footprints (avg sequence length and batch size)
3) Typical batch job concurrency and acceptable job completion window (e.g., 2 hours)

Proposed next step: a 60-minute dedicated-capacity sizing call where Marcus (our SE) will run through throughput scenarios, test vectors, and rough cost/instance mappings. Ben will cover contract/commit guidance.

Open slots this week (PST):
- Tue 12/01 09:30–10:30
- Tue 12/01 15:00–16:00
- Wed 12/02 08:00–09:00

If none of those fit, please paste a couple of alternatives or pick a slot here: https://calendly.com/redwood-inference/dedicated-sizing-30m (we can extend to 60m if needed).

I attached a short checklist that helps speed the session (redwood-sizing-checklist.pdf). If you can drop the initial telemetry/metering sheet (cloudledger-initial-metrics.xlsx) prior to the call, Marcus can sketch out a mock run.

Thanks — looking forward.

— Kim
Kimberly Park
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198

Attachment: redwood-sizing-checklist.pdf (1 page)
Attachment: cloudledger-initial-metrics.xlsx (stub)

From: Samir Kapadia <samir@cloudledger.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@cloudledger.com
Date: Mon, 29 Nov 2027 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Dedicated capacity sizing — scenario confirmation & proposed slots

Kim —

Thanks for the recap and the checklist. Quick answers below: 

1) Interactive: steady-state ~12 qps, 95th bursts up to 45 qps for ~10–15 minute windows during peak morning/EOQ reports.
2) KV/cache: average sequence len ~420 tokens; we expect per-request KV state ~1.2MB when expanded.
3) Batch reranking: two nightly jobs; each spawns ~4 worker processes, target completion window 90 minutes. Peak batch concurrency 320 qps sustained for the two-hour window.

We can make the telemetry sheet available by EOD Tuesday — attaching a trimmed export now.

Preferred slot: Tue 12/01 15:00–16:00 PST works for the CloudLedger team. Please include Marcus and Ben. Also loop in our infra lead (procurement@cloudledger.com will route to the right person).

Regards,
Samir
VP Engineering, CloudLedger
samir@cloudledger.com

Attachment: cloudledger-initial-metrics.xlsx (partial export)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 29 Nov 2027 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Dedicated capacity sizing — scenario confirmation & proposed slots

Samir — perfect, thanks for the numbers and the export. I’ve penciled Tue 12/01 15:00–16:00 PST on our side and sent a calendar invite.

Marcus — can you prepare:
- Two benchmark scenarios: 1) interactive production-like traffic (12 qps steady, 45 qps bursts), 2) batch rerank run at 320 qps for 2 hours.
- Rough instance/quantization options and an initial cost delta table (GPU families we expect to map to).
- A short checklist of traces/metrics we’ll ask for during the call so CloudLedger’s infra lead can surface them quickly.

Ben — I will flag the potential commit sizing and optional burst buffer talk in the invite so we don’t overrun.

Samir/procurement — if you’d like us to sign an NDA or have a vendor form we should complete before the call, send it over and I’ll loop legal.

Thanks all — calendar invite contains the draft agenda and the Drive link: https://drive.redwood.com/CL-2027-091/benchmarking-plan

Best,
Kim

- Workload A (interactive): sample trace generator, target p95 latency <200ms, config matrix for batch sizes [1,4,8] and quantization {FP16,4-bit}.
